title: Cache service in Node.js
idea: A cache service in Node.js puts an LRU in front of PostgreSQL: reads try the cache, a miss loads once, and writes update the database then invalidate.
points: Cache-aside: read the cache; on a miss, read the database and fill.
A `Map` keeps insertion order; delete then set a key to make it newest.
One shared promise per cold key stops parallel misses from stampeding PostgreSQL.
Interview follow-up: several instances hold copies; invalidate by message or short TTLs.

steps.caption: A read of P-1 reaches API 1. Its local LRU misses, so it queries PostgreSQL and keeps the row.
The next read of P-1 on API 1 is served from memory. PostgreSQL sees nothing.
A price change lands on API 2. It updates PostgreSQL and clears only its own cache.
API 1 still holds the old price. Its readers get stale data until the entry leaves.
Follow-up answer: API 2 publishes an invalidation through a shared channel, and API 1 drops its copy.

code.title: Cache-aside Express service
code.caption: An LRU of two products in front of a real PostgreSQL table, with stats, validation and invalidation on write.

walk.text: A product table with a CHECK on price, seeded with three rows.
LRU on a Map: a hit re-inserts the key; overflow drops the first key.
The repository counts database reads, so the demo can prove cache hits.
Service read: cache first, else one shared promise per key fills it.
Service write: update PostgreSQL first, then delete the cached copy.
Controllers validate with `zod`; the error middleware maps errors to 400, 404, 500.
Calls show a miss, a hit, a refused price, invalidation, eviction, then a parallel burst.

pitfalls: A read in flight during a write can cache the old row; keep a TTL.
Cache a not-found result only briefly, or new rows stay invisible.
An in-process cache dies with the process; never treat it as storage.

quiz.q: What does the last line of the service demo print?
options: DB reads for 3 parallel cold GETs: 3
DB reads for 3 parallel cold GETs: 0
DB reads for 3 parallel cold GETs: 1
quiz.why: P-1 was evicted, so the first request misses and stores a promise. Pending requests await it; later ones hit the filled cache. One query runs.

takeaway: Cache-aside with one load per key, and invalidate every copy on write.

starters: How would I add Redis as a second cache tier here?
